Internal helper: full-width punctuation in a map or labels string

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_fullwidth_args.Rd

Session 390 (the non-English probe; lean L2): a Chinese, Japanese or Korean input method types the full-width semicolon, equals sign and comma, which look like the plain ones and are other characters. jstats separates rules with the plain ones only, so jrelabel(d, Sex, labels = "1=M<fw;>2=F") made ONE label reading "M<fw;>2=F" for code 1, jdeclare_missing() kept the first code of two and gave it the rest as its label, and jrecode() and jencode() stopped in words that never named the character. This check runs at the front door of jrecode(), jencode(), jrelabel() and jdeclare_missing(): a string given to one of args (as typed, or held by a name) that holds one of the three outside a quoted label stops, naming what it found, with the call retyped with the plain characters – an ideographic space beside a replaced semicolon made a plain space too, since the parser's trim does not remove it. A label in quotes (ruling R17: the mark right after its =) is the user's text and is left alone, so a label that holds a full-width semicolon is still possible.

Usage

.jst_fullwidth_args(cl, mc, env, args, fn)

Arguments

cl

The call as typed (sys.call()).

mc

The matched call (match.call(expand.dots = TRUE)).

env

The caller's environment, where a name is looked up.

args

The arguments to read, e.g. c("map", "labels").

fn

Character(1); the user-facing function's name.

Value

Invisible NULL; stops when full-width punctuation is found.
